---
title: "Windows host"
description: "WinUSB with Zadig, and the Renesas limitation"
toc: true
---

`libusb` on Windows needs the WinUSB driver bound to a function of the
device. On boards that expose a vendor interface (the mbed boards — Portenta
H7, GIGA R1 WiFi, Nano 33 BLE, Nano RP2040 Connect — and the SAMD boards —
Zero, MKR family, Nano 33 IoT) this is a one-time setup with
[Zadig](https://zadig.akeo.ie/).

## Install WinUSB with Zadig, on the `UsbIo` interface only

1. Download and run [Zadig](https://zadig.akeo.ie/).
2. Enable *Options ▸ List All Devices*.
3. Select the entry named **UsbIo** — not the serial/COM port entry for the
   same board.
4. Click *Install Driver*.

::: {.callout-important}
## Bind WinUSB to `UsbIo` only

The board exposes both a CDC serial interface and, where the core supports
it, the dedicated vendor interface named **UsbIo** (class `FF`, subclass
`49`, protocol `4F`). Bind WinUSB to the **UsbIo** entry only. The COM port
keeps working exactly as before — `Serial.print()` debugging is unaffected —
because `arduino-io` never touches the CDC interface.
:::

## UNO R4 Minima and Nano R4 cannot be used on Windows

These two boards use the Renesas core, whose USB descriptors are fixed by the
core itself (`UsbIo` hooks a weak `tud_vendor_control_xfer_cb()` in TinyUSB,
with no `PluggableUSBModule` to add an interface through). There is no
function on the device for Zadig to bind WinUSB to without breaking the
serial port, so **Windows is not supported for these two boards at all** —
not "supported with extra setup," simply not usable with `arduino-io` on
Windows. Use [Linux](host-linux.qmd) or [macOS](host-macos.qmd) with one of
these boards, or pick a different board for a Windows bench — see [Supported
boards](boards.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
## Automatic binding: planned, not available

Automatic WinUSB binding through MS OS 2.0 descriptors — which would let
Windows bind the driver itself, without running Zadig — is a planned
follow-up in ArduinoDriver, not something available today. Zadig remains the
supported route for now.
:::

## Building `arduino-io`

Install Visual Studio 2022 with the *Desktop development with C++* workload,
and CMake 3.24 or newer. The same build as any other platform, choosing any
install prefix:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pbosetti/ArduinoDriver.git
cd ArduinoDriver
cmake -B build -DARDUINODRIVER_BUILD_TESTS=OFF
cmake --build build --config Release
cmake --install build --config Release --prefix <your folder>
```

The host driver and CLI build with MSVC (Visual Studio 2022 or newer) using
the same CMake project as Linux and macOS.
